extracted.intended_audience: independent nonfiction/documentary filmmakers (directors, producers, editors) seeking Sundance funding, labs, or support
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and selection priorities for filmmakers applying to the Sundance Institute Documentary Film Program (grants, labs, and special funds). Focuses on what kinds of nonfiction projects and artists the program supports and how projects are processed (applications, labs, invitations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Artful storytelling as transformative
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Sundance Documentary Film Program believes that artful storytelling can transform conversations and cultures.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DFP seeks projects and artists whose storytelling can shape public dialogue; this underpins their grantmaking and artist support philosophy rather than being a technical eligibility criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projects that elevate and advance cultural dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: DFP is committed to "nonfiction projects that elevate and advance cultural dialogue."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for work that contributes to cultural conversations and engages audiences beyond entertainment — described as part of the Documentary Fund’s mission and selection lens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential to generate social impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects should "have the potential to generate social impact around some of the most compelling issues of our time."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social impact is an explicit evaluative factor: projects addressing pressing societal issues are prioritized, especially those that can effect change or awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong artistic vision
rubrics_metrics.description: DFP seeks projects with a "strong artistic vision."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artistic merit is a core criterion; the program supports filmmakers with distinctive creative approaches and vision for their projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear and forward-going storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects should demonstrate "clear and forward-going storytelling."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are expected to articulate a coherent narrative trajectory and how the story will progress toward completion and audience engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial viability
rubrics_metrics.description: DFP looks for "financially viable nonfiction projects."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should present realistic financing and distribution plans or demonstrate that the project can be completed and reach audiences within feasible budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity and innovation; expanding the form
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference for projects that "expand the form through creativity and innovation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental or formally adventurous documentaries that push nonfiction form are encouraged; innovation is weighed alongside storytelling and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cinematic nonfiction on contemporary themes
rubrics_metrics.description: The program supports "cinematic documentaries on contemporary topics and themes."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works should be cinematic in approach and deal with timely, contemporary subject matter; this describes the topical and stylistic scope DFP favors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on human rights, social justice, civil liberties, freedom of expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentaries "that bear witness to issues of human rights, social justice, civil liberties, and freedom of expression" are highlighted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects dealing with these substantive areas are especially resonant with the program’s mission and are likely to be prioritized for funding and support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for labs and intensives (artist-centered, process-driven)
rubrics_metrics.description: DFP provides "artist-centered, process-driven support in the form of creative labs that support directors, producers, and editors."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feature nonfiction projects in production and post-production that would benefit from catalytic creative feedback, residential workshops, and ongoing customized support are good candidates for labs (Documentary Producers Lab, Edit Intensive).

rubrics_metrics.name: Residency and invitation requirements for specific programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Some opportunities (e.g., Documentary Edit Intensive) are "By invitation only."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should note that certain programs require invitation or selection from prior programs; others (Producers Lab) have residential sessions with specific dates/locations — check program timelines and application portals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Opportunity Funds target pressing socio-cultural issues and use general application
rubrics_metrics.description: "Projects selected for these opportunities will be fielded through our general Documentary Fund application."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying to the Documentary Fund, applicants may also be considered for partner-funded special opportunities (e.g., Gucci, Luminate, Kendeda) if their project aligns with those partners’ focus on socio-cultural issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonrecoupable funding and lifecycle support
rubrics_metrics.description: The Documentary Fund provides "nonrecoupable funding, supporting work... from development through release."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding does not require repayment and can support multiple stages of a film’s lifecycle; applicants should plan for long-term development and possible programmatic support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application and submission logistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are submitted through the Programs portal; specific cycles and opening dates are published (e.g., Documentary Fund Online Application Opening May 18th, 2026).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the online application process and timeframe; special funds and lab applications may have separate dates or be linked to the general Documentary Fund application. Contact dfp@sundance.org for inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alumni and cross-programmatic eligibility/benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees become part of the Sundance Alumni community and are "eligible for Sundance Institute cross-programmatic initiatives such as the Women@Sundance and Catalyst Forum (both are invitation only)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving a grant can unlock additional invitation-only opportunities and alumni services — applicants should understand grants can lead to further programmatic support and networking.
